plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with showy colored bracts surrounding small yellow flower clusters called cyathia. In its native range and in warm climates it flowers in short winter days, and it is widely grown as a potted holiday plant elsewhere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, grown outdoors in frost-free regions such as Southern California, Hawaii, and Mediterranean coasts
plants.funFact: The colorful 'petals' are actually modified leaves called bracts, and the plant needs about 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness nightly for several weeks to color up.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with flattened, segmented stems and arching, zygomorphic flowers at the tips. In its native Brazilian habitat it grows on tree branches and rocks in cool, humid mountain forests.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January)
plants.location: Native to the Organ Mountains of southeastern Brazil; popular as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: Flowering is triggered by short days and cool nights, and the plant can live for decades, with some specimens passed down through generations.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark leaves and delicate, often fragrant single or semi-double flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia, brightening gardens as most other plants go dormant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia's temperate regions
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce a camellia oil used in cooking and hair care in Japan.

plants.name: Nuytsia floribunda
plants.description: A large hemiparasitic tree that produces dense masses of bright orange flowers. Its roots tap into the roots of neighboring plants, including grasses and shrubs, to draw water and nutrients.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January), peaking around December
plants.location: Southwestern Western Australia, in sandy soils of woodlands and heathlands
plants.funFact: It is the world's largest mistletoe, and it is known to attack underground cables by mistaking them for roots, sometimes causing power outages.
